IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r8.claim: One Qur'anic sense is the sun's heat, as in the warning not to suffer its heat; the source also cites الشمس وضحاها.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r8.anchor: والثالث : حر الشمس . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في طه ] : ﴿ وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى ﴾

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p372/r10.claim: ضحى يضحى means to be exposed to the sun; Amr ibn Abi Rabia illustrates its contrast with coming indoors in the evening.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r1.claim: The paired assurances describe Paradise as free from weather hardship: hunger and shelter matter in cold, thirst and shade in heat.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r1.anchor: the hardships of cold nor of hot weather

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r2.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r2.claim: Some readers think thirst should be paired with hunger and the sun’s heat with shelter as a more apt formulation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r2.anchor: more apt to mention thirst with hunger

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r3.claim: Islahi rejects that objection as showing a lack of literary flair for Arabic, whose literature uses these paired conditions to evoke hot and cold weather.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p77/r3.anchor: this is the result of a deprivation of literary flair for Arabic

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p456/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p456/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p456/r3.claim: The cited pairing in Eden similarly links hunger with nakedness and thirst with exposure through shared semantic features.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p456/r3.anchor: فمن ذلك ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى وأنك لا تظمؤا فيها ولا تضحى

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.claim: Satan’s whisper exposes nakedness that had been hidden; the Quran and Bible both connect the couple’s disobedience with awareness of nakedness, followed by discussion of clothing.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r51.anchor: thereby to expose . . . their nakedness, which had been hidden from them

SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r1.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr read إنك with kasra; it may begin a new sentence or coordinate with the earlier إن.
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر و " إنك " بكسر الهمزة. والباقون بفتحها.

SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r2.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r2.claim: The other readers use fatḥa: the clause is an interpreted verbal noun coordinated with the subject of the earlier إن, whose predicate لك precedes it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r2.anchor: فلأنه عطف مصدرا مؤولا على اسم " إن " الأولى. والخبر " لك " المتقدم.

SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the wāw can stand for any governing element, not just أن; therefore it can occur before أن although إن أن would not be allowed.
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r3.anchor: فإن قلت: " إن " لا تدخل على " أن " فلا يقال: " إن أن زيدا منطلق " ، والواو نائبة عن " أن "

SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r4.claim: تضحى means to be exposed to the sun; the verse by Umar ibn Abi Rabi a supplies poetic usage.
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r4.anchor: وضحى يضحى أي: برز للشمس. قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة:

SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the verse names the feared miseries as negatives, rather than their positive opposites, so hearing the hardships will make Adam avoid their causes.
SAMIN-DURR:20:119/r5.anchor: وذكرها بلفظ النفي لنقائضها التي هي الجوع والعري والظمأ والضحو ليطرق

ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r3.claim: In the garden Adam is provided against hunger, nakedness, thirst, and exposure to the sun.
ASAD-NOTES:20:116/r3.anchor: Behold, it is provided for thee that thou shalt not hunger here or feel naked,[105]

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r1.claim: The question and answer gives lā taḍḥā the sense 'you will not sweat from intense heat' and cites a poetic line contrasting exposure to the sun and evening chill.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r1.anchor: أجاب: نعم، أما سمعت الشاعر يقول: رأت رجلا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r2.claim: The form ḍaḥā is unique in the Qur'an; other related forms name the forenoon or things occurring at that time.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r2.anchor: وحيدة الصيغة في القرآن. وجاء "الضحى" الوقت من النهار في آية الضحى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r3.claim: The author says 'not sweating from heat' is an approximation; the root refers to the period after sunrise and, in this verse, most likely means avoiding exposure to harmful sun.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r3.anchor: وتفسير "لا تضحى" بِ: لا تعرق من شدة الحر إنما يكون على وجه تقريب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r4.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ favors protection from harmful sun as the sense, rather than sweating; al-Ṭabarī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Rāghib give a similar exposure-to-sun interpretation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r4.anchor: قال الفراء في معنى الكلمة: لا تصيبك شكس مؤذية. وذكر في بعض التفسير: لا تعرق، والأول أشبه بالصواب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r5.speaker: المبرد
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains yaḍḥā as appearing in the sun and yakhsur as experiencing the cold of morning and evening, then cites the verse.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p332/r5.anchor: وقد فسره المبرد في الكامل بقوله: يضحى، يظهر للشمس، ويخصر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r1.claim: In the report from al-Mubarrad, Ibn ʿAbbās corrects Ibn al-Azraq's quotation of the poem: it says yakhsur, not yakhsar; Ibn al-Azraq had asked why he listened to a Qurayshi youth reciting it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r1.anchor: فقال ابن الأزرق: لله أنت يا ابن عباس، أنضرب إليك نسألك في الدين فتعرض، ويأتيك غلام من قريش

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad uses the verse to explain rare vocabulary in a literary recital, rather than treating the poem as Qur'anic analysis.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r2.anchor: وبعد أن علق "المبرد" على البيت وشرحه، استأنس له بقوله تعالى: {وَأَنَّكَ لَا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلَا تَضْحَى}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r3.claim: Among the transmissions of Ibn al-Azraq's questions available to the author, al-Mubarrad alone preserves this report about ʿUmar's poem.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r3.anchor: وسيأتي انفراد المبرد بهذا الخبر عن عمر ورائيته دون سائر الرواة لمسائل ابن الأزرق فيما وصل إلينا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī transmits an account in which Nāfiʿ sees Ibn ʿAbbās answering tafsir questions at the Meccan water basin, reproaches his boldness, and Ibn ʿAbbās begins to reply.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p290/r4.anchor: وأخرجها "أبو بكر ابن الأنباري" - ت 328 هـ - في مقدمات كتابه الجليل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p331/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p331/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p331/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the promise as not perspiring there from intense heat; the exchange with Ibn al-Azraq begins on this page.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p331/r9.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: لا [تعرق] فيها من شدة الحر. ولما سأله

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r1.speaker: نافع وعاصم برواية أبي بكر
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r1.claim: Nafi and Asim in Abu Bakr's narration read the initial hamza of wa-annaka with kasra.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r1.anchor: فقرأ نافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر: (وإنك) بكسر الألف

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs from Asim read the hamza with fatḥa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p251/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم: وأنك مفتوحة الألف

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p247#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p247#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p247#2/r3.claim: Not thirsting means not becoming thirsty, and not being exposed means not standing in the sun.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p247#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى لا تظمأ أي لا تعطش ولا تضحي أي لا تبرز للشمس

QIRAAT-ER:20:119:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:119:2#1/r1.speaker: ḥf
QIRAAT-ER:20:119:2#1/r1.claim: With kasra on hamza, inna is an independent emphatic assertion rather than subordinating anna, restructuring the clause.
QIRAAT-ER:20:119:2#1/r1.anchor: ḥf, mutawatir: Kasra on hamza: shifts from anna (subordinating) to inna (emphatic independent)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r1.claim: Ikrima glosses the promise that Adam will not thirst there as saying that he will not become thirsty.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r1.anchor: عن خصيف عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ لا تظمأ فيها ﴾ قال لا تعطش

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r2.claim: Ikrima explains that Adam will not be exposed to the sun there.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p20#6/r2.anchor: عن خصيف عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ لا تظمأ فيها ﴾ قال لا تعطش ﴿ ولا تضحى ﴾ قال لا تصيبك الشمس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r1.claim: The phrase means the sun does not strike Adam; Arabic also uses ḍaḥā/ḍaḥiya for exposure to sunlight.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r1.anchor: ولاتصيبك الشمس يقال : ضحا كسى وضحى كرضى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r2.claim: Some explain the phrase as not being exposed to the sun; the author says this second usage is also established in Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r2.anchor: ويقال ضحا ضحوا وضحوا وضحيا إذا برز لها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r3.speaker: عمرو بن أبي ربيعة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r3.claim: A line by ʿAmr ibn Abi Rabiʿa uses yaḍḥā for exposure to the sun, while the person grows cold in the evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r3.anchor: رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت فيضحى وأما بالعشي فيخصر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r4.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r4.claim: The explanation that the sun does not strike him is transmitted from ʿIkrima.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r5.claim: The four negations explain why the prohibition matters: the garden’s complete comforts make it vital to stay and avoid the cause of expulsion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r5.anchor: والجملة تعليل لما يوجبه النهي فإن اجتماع أسباب الراحة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r6.claim: Negating hunger, thirst, nakedness, and sun exposure recalls the feared afflictions more strongly than simply promising food, drink, clothing, and pleasant dwellings.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r6.anchor: والعدول عن التصريح بأن له عليه السلام فيها تنعما بفنون النعم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r7.claim: The negation means none of the four afflictions ever reaches him; he does not first suffer hunger and then obtain satiety, for example.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r7.anchor: أن لا يصيبه شئ من الأمور الأربعة اصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r8.claim: The permission to enjoy everything in the garden except the tree already expressed the positive side of this promise, so it is omitted here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r8.anchor: بما سوغ له من التمتع بجميع ما فيها سوى الشجرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r9.claim: One report says Adam asked whether the garden had food, clothing, drink, and shade; God answered with these four assurances. Al-Alusi doubts the report’s authenticity.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أن الاقتصار على ما ذكر لما وقع في سؤال آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r10.claim: Adam is singled out here for the same reason given above; another suggestion is that he was the one who asked about these needs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r10.anchor: ووجه افراده عليه السلام بما ذكر ما مر آنفا وقيل : كونه السائل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r11.claim: The arrangement pairs inner emptiness (hunger) with outer nakedness, then inner heat (thirst) with outer heat from the sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r11.anchor: وهي أن الجوع خلو الباطن والعرى خلو الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r12.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r12.claim: Al-Kashf says satiety and clothing are primary blessings, with drink and shade as complements, clarifying the favor; it also notes the distinction between inna laka and innaka.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r12.anchor: وفي الكشف إنما عدل إلى المنزل تنبيها على أن الشبع والكسوة أصلان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r13.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r13.claim: Al-Tibi says the four items are ordered by importance, expand the warning about expulsion, and by repeating fīhā and the negation allude to worldly hardship, since the garden is only for delight.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p271/r13.anchor: وفي تنسيق المذكورات الأربعة مرتبة هكذا مقدما ما هو الأهم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r1.speaker: الانتصاف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r1.claim: Al-Intisaf calls separating corresponding items qatʿ al-naẓīr ʿan al-naẓīr: separating each pair prevents two blessings seeming like one and emphasizes their number.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r1.anchor: وفي الانتصاف أن في الآية سرا بديعا من البلاغة يسمى قطع النظير عن النظير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r2.speaker: الكندي الأول
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r2.claim: The first Kindi’s verse separates riding for pleasure from urging horses to wheel back, and a woman’s embrace from drinking, to multiply his pleasures and boasts.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r2.anchor: الكندي الأول : كأني لم اركب جوادا للذة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r3.speaker: الكندي الآخر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r3.claim: The later Kindi likewise separates passing heroes from his smiling face and bright teeth, following the same rhetorical device.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r3.anchor: الكندي الآخر فقال : وقفت وما في الموت شك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r4.speaker: سيف الدولة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r4.claim: Sayf al-Dawla reproached the later Kindi for separating corresponding items; the poet answered that by this standard Imruʾ al-Qays would also be at fault, citing the first Kindi’s lines.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r4.anchor: سيف الدولة إذ قطع الشئ عن نظيره فقال له : إن كنت أخطأت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r5.claim: Al-Alusi questions whether the Kindi’s lines actually separate corresponding things, since riding and urging horses both express bravery, while the woman and wine share pleasure.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r5.anchor: في بيتي الأول : إنه جمع بين ركوب الخيل للذة والنزهة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r6.claim: He questions whether cadence requires this exact order; claiming the sequence serves the rhyme assumes without proof that another order could not do so.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r6.anchor: قصد تناسب الفواصل في الآية ظاهر في أنه لو عدل عن هذا الترتيب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r7.speaker: شيبه ونافع وحفص وابن سعدان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r7.claim: Shayba, Nafiʿ, Hafs, and Ibn Saʿdan read innaka with a kasra; most readers read annaka with a fatḥa.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r7.anchor: شيبه ونافع وحفص وابن سعدان ( انك ) بكسر الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r8.claim: With the majority’s fatḥa, the clause coordinates with an lā tajūʿa and becomes a verbal noun governed as the subject of inna; the two assertive particles do not conflict because they assert different relations.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r8.anchor: على أن العطف على أن لا تجوع وهو في تأويل مصدر اسم لأن

ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r9.claim: Wāw is not an assertive particle, so it does not create two assertions in one domain; the meaning emphasizes assured freedom from thirst and sun exposure.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p272/r9.anchor: حيث لم تكن حرفا موضوعا للتحقيق لم يلزم من دخولها اجتماع حر في التحقيق

ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says the reason for emphasizing assured freedom from thirst and sun exposure, unlike the preceding clause, still needs explanation and invites reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r1.anchor: بيان النكتة في عدم الاقتصار على بيان أن الثابت له عدم الظمأ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r2.claim: One says wāw stands for anna, but laka after it supplies a separator; al-Alusi calls this explanation plainly weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r2.anchor: وقيل إن الواو وإن كانت نائبة عن أن هنا إلا أنه يلاحظ

ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r3.claim: With the kasra reading, coordination is onto the first inna together with its clause, not just onto its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p273/r3.anchor: ولا يخفى عليك أن العطف على قراءة الكسر على أن الأولى مع معموليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r2.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read the hamza of وأنك with kasra, treating it as a new sentence.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر بكسر الألف على الاستئناف

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r3.claim: The other readers use fatḥa, coordinating this clause with ألا تجوع فيها.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r3.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالفتح نسقا على قوله: {ألا تجوع فيها}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r4.claim: The phrase means that Adam would not become thirsty in the Garden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r4.anchor: لا تظمأ} لا تعطش، {فيها ولا تضحى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r5.claim: Adam would not be exposed to the sun and harmed by its heat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r5.anchor: يعني: لا تبرز للشمس فيؤذيك حرها.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r6.speaker: عكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r6.claim: ʿIkrima says the sun and its harm would not reach Adam because the Garden has no sun and its people dwell in extended shade.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p299/r6.anchor: وقال عكرمة: لا تصيبك الشمس وأذاها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r1.claim: Together with the preceding verse, this recalls the Garden's four provisions: food, drink, clothing and shelter, without effort to obtain them or fear that they will disappear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r1.anchor: بيان وتذكير لما له في الجنة من أسباب الكفاية وأقطاب الكفاف التي هي الشبع والري والكسوة والسكن

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r2.claim: Mentioning the opposites of deprivation evokes the varieties of hardship from which Adam was warned.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r2.anchor: بذكر نقائضها، ليطرق سمعه بأصناف الشقوة المحذر عنها

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r3.claim: The conjunction substitutes for anna in its syntactic function, not as the particle in itself, so its entry upon anna is permissible.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r3.anchor: والعاطف وإن ناب عن أن لكنه ناب من حيث إنه عامل لا من حيث إنه حرف تحقيق

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r4.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r4.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read wa-innaka with kasra on the hamza; the other readers use fatḥa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:119/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر { وإنك لا تظمؤا } بكسر الهمزة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r5.claim: Thirst is an inner burning, while exposure is being struck by the sun's heat; neither inward nor outward heat will afflict Adam there.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p52/r5.anchor: أي لا يكون بحيث يصيبك حر الشمي

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Adam would suffer neither thirst nor heat in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى} قال: لا يصيبك فيها عطش ولا حر

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas separately glosses the two clauses as no thirst and no heat.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه في قوله: {لا تظمأ} قال: لا تعطش {ولا تضحى} قال: لا يصيبك فيها حر

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r6.claim: In a question from Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas explains the word as not sweating from intense sun, and cites an Arabic poem using يضحى for sun exposure.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله: {وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى} قال: لا تعرق فيها من شدة الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p605/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r7.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r7.claim: Ikrima glosses it as not being struck by the sun's heat.
DURR-FULL:v5p605/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولا تضحى} قال: لا يصيبك حر الشمس

BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r3.claim: He would not thirst because springs and rivers flow there continuously.
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r3.anchor: أي : لا تعطش لأن العيون والأنهار جارية على الدوام

BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r4.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r4.claim: Al-Raghib defines ẓamaʾ as the interval between drinks and the thirst that arises from it.
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r4.anchor: قال الراغب : الظمىء ما بين الشربتين والظمأ العطش الذي يعرض من ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r5.claim: He would not suffer the sun’s heat: there is no sun in the garden and its people rest in extended shade; ḍaḥā means going out exposed to the sun.
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r5.anchor: {ولا تضحى} أي : لا يصيبك حر الشمس في الجنة إذ لا شمس فيها وأهلها في ظل ممدود يقال ضحى الرجل للشمس

BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r6.claim: The fatḥa on anna introduces a clause coordinated with an lā tajūʿa; separating thirst from hunger prevents treating their absence as one blessing, as the separation of nakedness and sun exposure does.
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r6.anchor: وأن بالفتح مع ما في حيزها عطف على أن لا تجوع وفصل الظمأ دفعا لتوهم أن نفيهما نعمة واحدة وكذا الحال في الجمع بين العرى والضحو

BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r7.claim: The inward reading says the abiding garden, though the neighborhood of God, also serves the animal self as a pasture where it enjoys food, drink, clothing, and sexual partners, as in worldly life.
BURSEVI:v5p335#2/r7.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى أن الجنة وإن كانت باقية وهي جوار الحق لكنها مرتعة من مراتع النفس البهيمية الحيوانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.claim: Adam’s creation and the angels’ prostration were already related in al-Baqara and al-Aʿraf; Ibn ʿĀshūr focuses here on what is distinctive in this sura’s wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p320/r1.anchor: قصة خلق آدم وسجود الملائكة له وإباء الشيطان من السجود تقدمت في سورة البقرة وسورة الأعراف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r3.claim: تضحى is a present verb from ضحي, to be exposed to the sun’s heat during the forenoon; that heat is just beginning to intensify.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r3.anchor: و { تضحى } مضارع ضحي : كرضي ، إذا أصابه حر الشمس في وقت الضحى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r4.claim: The point is freedom from conditions that upset one’s constitution; the mention of sun exposure also implies freedom from cold.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r4.anchor: والمعنى : لا يصيبك ما ينافر مزاجك ، فالاقتصار على انتفاء الضحو هنا اكتفاء ، أي ولا تصرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r5.claim: Adam did not experience hunger, nakedness, thirst, or sun exposure directly; he knew their realities through the teaching of all the names.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r5.anchor: وآدم لم يعرف الجوع والعرى والظمأ والضحو بالوجدان ، وإنما عرفها بحقائقها ضمن تعليمه الأسماء كلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r6.claim: These four absences identify basic human needs and foreshadow that securing them will occupy people’s future lives; conditions accompanying creation signal the created being’s defining components.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r6.anchor: وجمع له في هذا الخبر أصول كفاف الإنسان في معيشته إيماء إلى أن الاستكفاء منها سيكون غاية سعي الإنسان في حياته المستقبلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r7.claim: The author likens this foreshadowing to the Israʾ report in which the Prophet chose milk over wine and was told that choosing wine would have led his community astray.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r7.anchor: كما ورد في حديث الإسراء من توفيق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لاختيار اللبن على الخمر فقيل له : لو اخترت الخمر لغوت أمتك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r8.claim: Hunger pairs with nakedness because both describe missing protection from bodily harm inside or outside; thirst pairs with sun heat as inner and outer heat, explaining why the apparent parallel pairs are separated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p321/r8.anchor: وقد قرن بين انتفاء الجوع واللباس في قوله { ألا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى ، وقرن بين انتفاء الظمأ وألم الجسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r1.claim: The cited poetic contrast and the examples of Imruʾ al-Qays and Abu al-Tayyib illustrate how separating matched terms can create a more striking antithesis than grouping obvious parallels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r1.anchor: ومعنى هذا أن امرؤ القيس خالف مقتضى الظاهر في جمع شيئين مشتهري المناسبة فجمع شيئين متناسبين مناسبة دقيقة ، وأن أبا الطيب خالف مقتضى الظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r2.claim: God’s gifts are presented through the absence of their opposites so Adam hears the names of kinds of misery as a warning to avoid losing his blessings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r2.anchor: وجعلت المنة على آدم بهذه النعم مسوقة في سياق انتفاء أضدادها ليطرق سمعه بأسامي أصناف الشقوة تحذيرا منها لكي يتحامى من يسعى إلى إرزائه منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r3.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r3.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read وإنك with kasra, coordinating a full clause with the preceding clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع ، وأبو بكر عن عاصم { وإنك لا تظمأ } بكسر همزة ( إن ) عطفا للجملة على الجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r4.speaker: الباقون
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r4.claim: The other readers use fatḥa in وأنك, coordinating a clause constituent with ألا تجوع.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r4.anchor: وأنك بفتح الهمزة عطفا على ألا تجوع عطف المفرد على المفرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r5.claim: Both readings emphasize the same four protections with إن and its counterpart, while varying the syntactic style.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p324/r5.anchor: وقد حصل تأكيد الجميع على القراءتين ب ( إن ) وبأختها ، وبين الأسلوبين تفنن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.claim: Adam is promised complete, lasting provision in Paradise: no hunger, nakedness, thirst, or harmful sun exposure; ḍuḥā means exposure to the sun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r1.anchor: المعنى إن لك يا آدم نعمة تامة وعطية مستمرة أن لا يصيبك جوع ولا عري ولا ظمأ ولا بروز للشمس يؤذيك وهو الضحاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.speaker: نافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.claim: Nafi and Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission read وإنك with kasra on the initial alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر «وإنك لا تظمأ» بكسر الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r3.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r3.claim: The other readers and Hafs from Asim read وأنك with fatḥa on the initial alif.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وحفص عن عاصم «وأنك» بفتح الألف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r4.claim: The verse pairs hunger with nakedness and thirst with sun exposure, dispersing the usual associations; Arabic poetry also uses such arrangement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r4.anchor: وجعل الله تعالى الجوع في هذه الآية مع العري والظمأ مع الضحاء وكأن عرف الكلام أن يكون الجوع مع الظمأ المتناسب والعري مع الضحاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r5.claim: Imru al-Qays's lines are cited for associations between horseback riding for pleasure and embracing a woman.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب بعض الأدباء إلى أن بيتي امرئ القيس حافظة لنسب وأن ركوب الخيل للصيد وغيره من الملاذ يناسب تبطن الكاعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r6.claim: A poet's use of فيضحى exemplifies exposure to sunlight.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p67#2/r6.anchor: رأت رجلا أما إذا الشمس عارضت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r2.claim: One group reads وأنك with fatḥa and coordinates it with ألا تجوع.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r2.anchor: وقرأت فرقة «وأنك» بفتح الألف عطفا على قوله ألا تجوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p68/r3.claim: Another group reads وإنك with kasra and coordinates it with إن لك.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs from ʿAsim read the opening hamza of wa-annaka with fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r1.anchor: قر أابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r2.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r2.claim: Nafiʿ and Abu Bakr from ʿAsim read the opening hamza with kasra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابو بكر عن عاصم وإنك بكسر الألف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r3.claim: Abu ʿAli explains that the fatḥa coordinates this clause with the earlier “anna laka,” while kasra begins a new sentence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي من فتح حمله على أن لك أن لا تجوع وأن لك أن لا تظمأ ومن كسر استأنف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r4.claim: Tazmaʾ means to thirst; the verb is used of a man who becomes thirsty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r4.anchor: أي لا تعطش يقال ظمئ الرجل ظمأ فهو ظمآن أي عطشان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r5.claim: Tadḥā means being exposed to the sun and its heat; Paradise has no sun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p329#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى لا تضحى لا تبرز للشمس فيصيبك حرها لأنه ليس في الجنة شمس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320#2/r2.claim: Thirst and exposure to the sun are paired: thirst is heat within, while dahwa is heat on the outside.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p320#2/r2.anchor: وهذان أيضا متقابلان، فالظمأ: حر الباطن، وهو العطش. والضحى: حر الظاهر

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r10.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r10.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr from Asim read وإنك with a kasra as a new sentence; the others use a fatha to coordinate it with ألا تجوع.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r10.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر عن عاصم: وإنك لا تظمأ بكسر الهمزة على الاسنتئناف

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r11.claim: The other readers use a fatha on إنك, coordinating it with the subject of ألا تجوع.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالفتح عطفا على اسم (ألا تجوع)

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r12.claim: Ẓamaʾ, with hamza, means thirst; ẓamʾ is also the interval between drinks, while ẓamā without hamza means thinness of the gums.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r12.anchor: الظمأ مهموز: ش هو العطش، ظمئت ظمأ، وما بين الشربتين ظمء، والظمى غير مهموز: قلة دم اللثة

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r13.claim: Duha is the day’s beginning; ḍaḥiya means to be exposed to the sun, and the root also describes what appears or lies exposed.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r13.anchor: والضحى: ابتداء النهار، وضحى الرجل تعرض لحر الشمس، وضحا يضحو مثله، واضح يا رجل ابرز للشمس

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r14.claim: The word family also denotes morning, an exposed district or road, and acting openly; sacrifice names derive from slaughter at forenoon and have several forms.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r14.anchor: ومنه: الضحى: الغداة، وضحا الطريق يضحو ضحوا: [بدا] وظهر

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r15.speaker: الفراء
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r15.claim: Al-Farra says أضحى is feminine but can be masculine when it means the day; its basic sense is exposure.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r15.anchor: قال الفراء: الأضحى مؤنثة وقد تذكر، يذهب بها إلى اليوم، وأصله: البروز

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r16.speaker: ابن عرفة
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r16.claim: Ibn Arafa says anything exposed rather than sheltered or shaded is described as ḍāḥ.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r16.anchor: قال ابن عرفة: يقال لكل ما كان بارزا من غير ما يكنه ويظله: أنه ضاح

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r17.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r17.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains the rain prayer report that the land was exposed as meaning the sun had scorched it through drought.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r17.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: أي: أضحت الشمس، وضحيت ضحوا فيها

JISHUMI:v7p4754/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r18.speaker: ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r18.claim: They explain the promise as no thirst and no exposure to the sun’s heat; another view says Paradise has no sun, only light.
JISHUMI:v7p4754/r18.anchor: أي لا تعطش ولا يصيبك حر الشمس، عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، وقتادة. وقيل: ليس في الجنة شمس

MUQATIL:20:119-122/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r1.claim: In Paradise, Adam would not become thirsty.
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r1.anchor: { وأنك لا تظمأ فيها } يعنى لا تعطش فى الجنة

MUQATIL:20:119-122/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r2.claim: The sun's heat would not afflict and harm him there.
MUQATIL:20:119-122/r2.anchor: فى الجنة { ولا تضحى } [آية: 119] يقول: لا يصيبك حر الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr read “and that you” with kasra, linking it to the preceding “that”; other readers use fatḥa, linking it to “that you do not hunger.”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وإنك ﴾ بالكسر نافع وابو بكر عطفا على ان الآولى وغيرهما بالفتح عطفا على أن لا تجوع

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r2.claim: There is no thirst in the Garden because drinks are available.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r3.claim: Adam is not exposed to the sun’s heat because the Garden has no sun and its inhabitants have extended shade.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p70#3/r3.anchor: لا يصيبك حر الشمس إذ ليس فيها شمس فاهلها فى ظل ممدود

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r14.anchor: { وأنك لا تظمأ فيها } أي لا تعطش. والظمأ العطش.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r15.claim: تضحى means exposure to the sun's heat; Paradise has no sun, only extended shade between dawn and sunrise.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:116-119/r15.anchor: أي تبرز للشمس فتجد حرها. إذ ليس في الجنة شمس، إنما هو ظل ممدود،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r1.claim: Abu al-Aliyah describes the daylight of Paradise as lasting about the time people pray the dawn prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r1.anchor: قال أبو العالية: نهار الجنة هكذا: وأشار إلى ساعة المصلين صلاة الفجر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r2.claim: Abu Zayd says the road becomes visible and apparent when it is exposed to the sun.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r2.anchor: قال أبو زيد: ضحا الطريق يضحو ضحوا إذا بدا لك وظهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r3.claim: The verb ضحيت can mean sweating, or coming out into the sun; both forms ضحيت and ضحيت are reported, with أضحى as the future in either usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r3.anchor: وضحيت وضحيت بالكسر ضحا عرقت. وضحيت أيضا للشمس ضحاء ممدود برزت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r4.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r4.claim: Umar ibn Abi Rabiʿa's line uses يضحى for being exposed to the sun, supporting the lexical explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r4.anchor: قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة: رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت فيضحى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar told a pilgrim who had shaded himself, “Expose yourself for the One for whom you entered ihram”; hadith transmitters vocalize أضح as أضحيت.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث أن ابن عمر رأى رجلا محرما قد استظل، فقال: أضح لمن أحرمت له.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿi corrects the wording to اِضْحَ from ضحيت أضحى, meaning to expose oneself to the sun; he cites the verse and a poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r6.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: إنما هو اضح لمن أحرمت له بكسر الألف وفتح الحاء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r7.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses ضحيت for coming out into sunlight, as shown by the contrast with a shrinking shadow.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r7.anchor: ضحيت له كي أستظل بظله إذا الظل أضحى في القيامة قالصا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو والكوفيون إلا عاصما في رواية أبي بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r8.claim: Abu ʿAmr and the Kufans except ʿAsim in Abu Bakr's transmission read وأنك with an open hamza, coordinating it with ألا تجوع.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والكوفيون إلا عاصما في رواية أبي بكر عنه «وأنك» بفتح الهمزة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r9.claim: With the open hamza, وأنك may also be nominative by coordination with the syntactic position, meaning that you will not thirst there.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع رفع عطفا على الموضع، والمعنى: ولك أنك لا تظمأ فيها

QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r10.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r10.claim: The remaining readers use a kasra on إنك, treating it as a new sentence or coordinating it with إن لك.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:118/r10.anchor: الباقون بالكسر على الاستئناف، أو على العطف على «إن لك».

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r5.claim: The phrase wa-annaka is read with either fatḥ or kasrah; fatḥ coordinates with an lā tajūʿa. Though an does not normally precede another an, the wāw can stand for any governing particle, not only an.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r5.anchor: قرىء وإنك بالفتح والكسر ووجه الفتح العطف على أن لا تجوع فيها

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r6.claim: Satiety, drinking, clothing, and shade are the four pillars of human well-being; God grants them in the Garden without earning or effort.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r6.anchor: الشبع والري والكسوة والإكتنان في الظل هي الأقطاب التي يدور عليها أمر الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r7.claim: The blessings are expressed by negating their opposites so Adam hears forms of hardship and becomes especially wary of the cause that would bring them.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r7.anchor: وذكرها بلفظ النفي لأضدادها التي هي الجوع والعري والظمأ والضحى ليطرق سمعه شيئا من أصناف الشقوة

RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.claim: Freedom from hunger, nakedness, thirst, and sun exposure explains the misery mentioned in the preceding warning.
RAZI-FULL:v22p108/r8.anchor: تفسير الشقاء المذكور في قوله : { فتشقى }

QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r14.claim: Adam had every comfort in Paradise but failed to recognize the value of safety until the prior allotment unfolded.
QUSHAYRI:v2p277/r14.anchor: أوثر بكل وجه ؛ فلم يعرف قدر العافية والسلامة ، إلى أن جرى ما هو محكوا به من سابق القسمة

QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r1.claim: Adam appreciated Paradise only after worldly hunger, thirst, and affliction came; he wept at each new trial, and Gabriel conveyed God's greeting and asked why.
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r1.anchor: وكان آدم عليه السلام إذا تجدد له نوع نم البلاء أخذ في البكاء ، وجبريل عليه السلام - يأتي ويقول : ربك يقرئك السلام ويقول : لم تبكي

QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r2.claim: Gabriel's question reminded Adam of the promised freedom from thirst, heat, and other hardships in Paradise.
QUSHAYRI:v2p278/r2.anchor: أهذا لاذي قلت : { وأنك لا تظمؤا فيها ولآ تضحى }

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r4.claim: The absence of hunger, nakedness, thirst, and sun's heat evokes the Garden's ease, contrasted with worldly hardship after yielding to Satan.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r4.anchor: Thus, the references in v. 118 to being neither hungry nor naked, and in v. 119 to neither being thirsty nor experiencing the sun’s heat

STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.claim: The commentary points to other accounts of the warning, Satan's deception, the fall, and Adam and Eve's remorse.
STUDYQURAN:20:117/r5.anchor: For other accounts of Adam and Eve’s being warned by God, Satan’s deceiving them, their fall from Paradise, and their remorse over their actions

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r2.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r2.claim: Some readers of Medina and Kufa read wa-innaka with kasra, coordinating it with the earlier إن لك.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r2.anchor: قرأ ذلك بعض قراء المدينة والكوفة بالكسر: (وإنك) على العطف على قوله: {إن لك}

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r3.speaker: بعض قراء المدينة وعامة قراء الكوفة والبصرة
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r3.claim: Some Medinan readers and the majority of readers in Kufa and Basra read wa-annaka with fatḥa, coordinating it with ألا تجوع فيها.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r3.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض قراء المدينة وعامة قراء الكوفة والبصرة: وأنك، بفتح ألفها عطفا بها على «أن»

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the fatḥa reading because it coordinates both promised comforts; he still considers the kasra reading plausible.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r4.anchor: فهذه القراءة أعجب القراءتين إلي، لأن الله تبارك وتعالى ذكره وعد ذلك آدم حين أسكنه الجنة

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r5.claim: In the Garden, Adam will not suffer thirst for as long as he remains there.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r5.anchor: وعنى بقوله: {لا تظمأ فيها} [طه: 119] لا تعطش في الجنة ما دمت فيها

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r6.claim: To be deprived of exposure to the sun means Adam will not suffer its heat in the Garden.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r6.anchor: لا تظهر للشمس فيؤذيك حرها، كما قال ابن أبي ربيعة: [البحر الطويل]

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r7.speaker: ابن أبي ربيعة
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Rabiʿa's verse uses yaḍḥā of a man exposed to the sun, supporting al-Tabari's gloss of the word.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r7.anchor: كما قال ابن أبي ربيعة: [البحر الطويل] رأت رجلا أما إذا الشمس عارضت … فيضحى وأما بالعشي فيخصر

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the promise as freedom from thirst and heat, and in another report from heat and harm.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى} [طه: 119] يقول: لا يصيبك فيها عطش ولا حر

TAB-FULL:v16p187/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses the phrase as protection from the sun.
TAB-FULL:v16p187/r9.anchor: عن خصيف، عن سعيد بن جبير، {لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى} [طه: 119] قال: لا تصيبك الشمس

TAB-FULL:v16p188/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p188/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p188/r1.claim: Qatada explains wa-la taḍḥā as not being struck by the sun.
TAB-FULL:v16p188/r1.anchor: عن قتادة {ولا تضحى} [طه: 119] قال: لا تصيبك الشمس

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r7.claim: Ḍaḥā means to be struck by or exposed to sunlight; lacking sun exposure means no heat that would make shelter from heat or cold necessary.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r7.anchor: يقال ضحى يضحى كسعى يسعى ضحوا وضحيا إذا أصابته الشمس أو برز لها

TABATABAI:20:117-122/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r8.claim: The four comforts use an ordered wrap-and-unfold arrangement for rhyme; their unmarked order would be hunger, thirst, nakedness, then sun exposure.
TABATABAI:20:117-122/r8.anchor: وقد رتبت الأمور الأربعة على نحو اللف والنشر المرتب لرعاية الفواصل

TABRISI:20:124/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r1.speaker: نافع، أبو بكر
TABRISI:20:124/r1.claim: Nafi and Abu Bakr read the particle before the thirst clause with kasra; the other readers read it with fatha.
TABRISI:20:124/r1.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو بكر وإنك لا تظمؤ بالكسر والباقون أنك بالفتح

TABRISI:20:124/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r2.claim: With fatha, the clause continues the promise that Adam will not hunger; joining two adjacent particles of similar meaning is avoided, but separation permits it. With kasra, the clause begins anew.
TABRISI:20:124/r2.anchor: من قرأ بالفتح فتقديره أن لك أن لا تجوع فيها وأن لك أنك لا تظمأ ولا يجوز أن تقول أن أنك

TABRISI:20:124/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r5.claim: The verb for being exposed in the sun means to be out in sunlight.
TABRISI:20:124/r5.anchor: ضحى الرجل يضحى ضحى إذا برز للشمس

TABRISI:20:124/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، سعيد بن جبير، قتادة
TABRISI:20:124/r12.claim: They explain that Adam would neither thirst nor suffer the sun’s heat; Paradise has no sun, only light, brightness, and extended shade.
TABRISI:20:124/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير وقتادة قالوا ليس في الجنة شمس وإنما فيها ضياء ونور وظل ممدود

TABRISI:20:124/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r13.claim: One explanation pairs thirst with sun exposure because heat causes thirst, and pairs hunger with nakedness as inner and outer deprivation.
TABRISI:20:124/r13.anchor: إن الظمأ أكثر ما يكون من شدة الحر والحر إنما يكون من الضحى وهو الانكشاف للشمس

TABRISI:20:124/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124/r14.claim: Alternatively, Arabic pairs two expressions and trusts listeners to match each with its semantic counterpart; the cited Imru’ al-Qays verse can be read this way.
TABRISI:20:124/r14.anchor: إن العرب تلف الكلامين بعضهما ببعض اتكالا على علم المخاطب وأنه يرد كل واحد منهما إلى ما يشاكله

TABRISI:20:124#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:124#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:124#2/r1.claim: Imru’ al-Qays’s verse scrambles expected pairings, while Abd Yaghuth supplies the more fitting pairs; the former can still be read under the first explanation.
TABRISI:20:124#2/r1.anchor: وكان حقه أن يقول كما قال عبد يغوث: كأني لم أركب جوادا ولم أقل

THALABI:v6p263/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r13.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read the hamza of wa-annaka with kasra as a new sentence; the others read it with fatḥa, coordinating it with the preceding clauses.
THALABI:v6p263/r13.anchor: قرأ نافع بكسر الألف على الاستئناف، ومثله روى أبو بكر عن عاصم

THALABI:v6p263/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r14.claim: The garden protects Adam from thirst.
THALABI:v6p263/r14.anchor: لا تظمؤا بعطش فيها ولا تضحى

THALABI:v6p263/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p263/r15.claim: Taḍḥā means being exposed to the sun and hurt by its heat.
THALABI:v6p263/r15.anchor: ولا تضحى تبرز للشمس فيؤذيك حرها

THALABI:v6p263/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r16.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
THALABI:v6p263/r16.claim: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa's poem contrasts a man exposed to the sun at midday with shelter in the evening, illustrating taḍḥā.
THALABI:v6p263/r16.anchor:
قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة:
رأت رجلا أما إذا الشمس عارضت

THALABI:v6p263/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p263/r17.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v6p263/r17.claim: ʿIkrima explains taḍḥā as being struck by the sun.
THALABI:v6p263/r17.anchor: عن عكرمة: ولا تضحى ولا تصيبك الشمس

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#3/r1.claim: The phrase means that sunlight will not strike you.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p283#3/r1.anchor: ولا تضحى} أي لا يصيبك الضحى، وهو الشمس (3) .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq says wa-annaka is accusative, coordinated with allā tajūʿa; it may also be nominative because the sense is “you do not thirst,” explaining the clause after inna.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: {وأنك} في موضع نصب نسقا على قوله: {ألا تجوع} ويجوز أن تكون في موضع رفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r2.claim: A reading with kasra, wa-innaka, begins a new clause coordinated with the preceding sentence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ: وإنك بالكسر على الاستئناف، وعطف جملة كلام على جملة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r3.claim: Ḍaḥā means that a person is exposed to the sun and its heat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r3.anchor: يقال: ضحا الرجل إذا برز للشمس فأصابه حرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r4.speaker: النضر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r4.claim: Al-Naḍr gives the form ḍaḥā li-l-shams, yaḍḥā, ḍaḥwan.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī gives the forms ḍaḥaytu li-l-shams and ḍaḥītu, both with the imperfect aḍḥā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: (ضحيت للشمس، وضحيت، أضحى منهما جميعا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r6.speaker: شمر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r6.claim: Shammar reports the forms ḍaḥiya/yaḍḥā, ḍaḥyan, ḍaḥā/yaḍḥū, and ḍaḥwan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r6.anchor: وحكى شمر: (ضحي، يضحى، ضحيا، وضحا، يضحو، ضحوا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj cites a line about a man who is exposed to the sun at midday and becomes chilled by evening; it illustrates yaḍḥā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r7.anchor: وأنشد الزجاج (¬4): رأت رجلا أما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيضحى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r8.claim: In al-Ḍaḥḥāk's report, Ibn ʿAbbās says Adam would not suffer thirst or heat as people do in this world.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك يقول: (لا تعطش فيها كما يعطش أهل الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r9.claim: In ʿIkrima's report, Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as not being struck by the sun.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r9.anchor: وقال في رواية عكرمة: (لا تصيبك الشمس)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r10.claim: In reports through al-Wālibī and ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says there is neither heat nor thirst in Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r10.anchor: وقال في رواية الوالبي، وعطاء: (لا يصيبك فيها حر ولا عطش)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r11.claim: Adam is not exposed to the sun's harmful heat; Paradise has no sun, only extended shade.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p546/r11.anchor: ليس في الجنة شمس إنما هو ظل ممدود

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:119-122/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:119-122/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:119-122/r1.claim: Not being exposed to the sun means its heat will not harm you.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:119-122/r1.anchor: { ولا تضحى } أي: لا يؤذيك حر الشمس. وقوله:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r8.claim: In Paradise, Adam will not thirst.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r8.anchor: {وأنك لا تظمأ فيها} [طه: 119] لا تعطش فيها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r9.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r9.claim: Qatadah says Adam will not be struck by the sun there.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p283/r9.anchor: {ولا تضحى} [طه: 119] قال قتادة: لا تصيبك فيها شمس.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p284/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p284/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p284/r1.claim: The phrase means that the heat of the sun will not reach Adam.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p284/r1.anchor: {ولا تضحى} [طه: 119] يعني: لا يصيبك حر شمس.

BURHAN:v3p464/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p464/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p464/r1.claim: The worldly list of desires is paired with six corresponding afterlife blessings; the contrast preserves desire and sustenance at both ends, places spouses in the afterlife order, and culminates in God's approval.
BURHAN:v3p464/r1.anchor: قابل الجنات والأنهار والخلد والأزواج والتطهير والرضوان بإزاء النساء في الدنيا وختم بالحرث وهما طرفان متشابهان

BURHAN:v3p464/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p464/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p464/r2.claim: Although hunger and nakedness, then thirst and exposure to the sun, may seem mismatched, the pairings cover inner and outer affliction: hunger is inward pain, while midday heat affects the exterior.
BURHAN:v3p464/r2.anchor: والمدقق يرى هذا الكلام في أعلى مراتب الفصاحة لأن الجوع ألم الباطن والضحى موجب لحرارة الظاهر

BURHAN:v3p464/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p464/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p464/r3.claim: The author invokes a famous anecdote about al-Mutanabbi and Sayf al-Dawla, quoting a line about standing before death, as a related illustration of this rhetorical pairing.
BURHAN:v3p464/r3.anchor: وهاهنا موضع الحكاية المشهورة بين المتنبي وسيف الدولة لما أنشده

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r1.claim: Calling someone all people or worth a thousand men attributes to him a sum of virtues found among others without denying those virtues to them.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r1.anchor: تدعي له جميع المعاني الشريفة المتفرقة في الناس من غير أن تبطل تلك المعاني ، وتنفيها عن الناس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r2.claim: Calling someone simply the brave or generous claims unique excellence, making others' courage or generosity seem unworthy of the name; the cited poems illustrate this hyperbole.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p156/r2.anchor: فإنك تدعي له أنه قد انفرد بحقيقة الشجاعة ، وأنه قد أوتي فيها مزية ، وخاصية لم يؤتها أحد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r1.claim: The proposed reading that present tears secure lasting union and future tearlessness fails: it makes the speaker seek present crying in order to become like an eye incapable of tears.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r1.anchor: فإن ذلك لا يستقيم ويستتب لأنه يوقعه في التناقض ويجعله كأنه قال : أحتمل البكاء لهذا الفراق عاجلا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r2.claim: A dry eye is not a recognized sign of joy or contentment, so it cannot carry the proposed meaning of lasting happiness.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r2.anchor: جمود العين دليل سرور ، وأمارة غبطة وكناية عن أن الحال حال فرح

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r3.claim: With sound composition, meaning reaches the heart as the wording reaches the ear; faulty composition delays understanding, and extreme obscurity becomes verbal complexity that consumes meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r3.anchor: كان وصول المعنى إلى قلبك تلو وصول اللفظ إلى سمعك . وإذا كان على خلاف ما ينبغي وصل اللفظ

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r4.speaker: البحتري
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r4.claim: Asked whether Muslim or Abu Nuwas was the better poet, al-Buhturi chose Abu Nuwas and said judging poetry belongs to practiced poets, not scholars who study it without making it.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p210/r4.anchor: البحتري قال حين سئل عن مسلم وأبي نواس : أيهما أشعر ؟ فقال : أبو نواس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r1.claim: Eloquence cannot belong to wording independently of meaning; likewise, brevity cannot be a property of bare wording, since brevity means few words indicate much meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r1.anchor: لا معنى للإيجاز إلا أن يدل بالقليل من اللفظ على الكثير من المعنى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r2.claim: Word meanings cannot simply be increased or reduced; apparent concision comes when one meaning indirectly points to another that would take many words to state directly.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r2.anchor: يتوصل بدلالة المعنى على المعنى إلى فوائد لو أنه أراد الدلالة عليها باللفظ لاحتاج إلى لفظ كثير

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r3.claim: Prestige, repetition, and inherited consensus can make even an obvious error seem authoritative, discouraging experts from examining the flawed theory that eloquence resides in wording alone.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p335/r3.anchor: ولا كان يرسخ في النفوس هذا الرسوخ ، وتتشعب عروقه هذا التشعب

ITQAN:v3p255/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p255/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p255/r5.claim: The paired Eden expressions are cross-associated: hunger and nakedness share emptiness, while thirst and exposure to noon share burning heat.
ITQAN:v3p255/r5.anchor: أتى بالجوع مع العري وبابه أن يكون مع الظمأ وبالضحى مع الظمأ وبابه أن يكون مع العري

ITQAN:v2p349/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p349/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p349/r7.claim: لا تضحى means not to sweat in the sun's heat; an unnamed poet's line is cited for يضحى.
ITQAN:v2p349/r7.anchor: قال لا تعرق فيها من شدة حر الشمس قال وهل تعرف العرب ذلك قال نعم أما سمعت الشاعر يقول

ITQAN:v2p343/r27.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r27.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r27.claim: Lā taẓmaʾ means you will not thirst.

ITQAN:v2p343/r28.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p343/r28.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p343/r28.claim: Wa-lā taḍḥā means you will not be exposed to heat.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r12.claim: One group reads the Quranic clause with open وأنك, attaching it to the preceding إن لك.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r12.anchor: على إن لك وقد قرئ هذا الحرف على وجهين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r13.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r13.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r13.claim: Another group reads the phrase with closed وإنك as a new independent statement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنأبوابأن)#498/r13.anchor: لا تظمأ فيها @QE@ وقال بعضهم وأنك
